title: A2A-to-MCP authority relay — blind reproduction challenge

official_sources.title: Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization concept paper

tasks.scenario: A recorded A2A 1.0 read reaches the exact MCP resource and tool bound to the same subject, actor, task, tenant, current Agent Card digest, live one-use delegation, audience-bound MCP token, current policy epoch, and available monitor.
Every relay binding matches a recorded read except the selected A2A protocol version is 0.3 while the authority profile requires 1.0.
The relay credential is current and correctly signed, but the authenticated subject differs from the subject bound to the A2A task and MCP authorization envelope.
All identities and destinations match, but the one-use delegation identifier was already consumed by an earlier A2A-to-MCP request.
The A2A request is authorized for a shipment-status read, but the translated MCP call targets a customer-record resource outside the exact resource set carried by the authority envelope.
The A2A service token is valid for its original audience and is forwarded unchanged to the downstream MCP resource server, whose resource indicator and audience are different.
All static relay bindings match, but the independent monitor required by the active authority lease is unavailable before MCP dispatch.

The relay requests a prepared external change whose profile requires recorded human approval, but the approval identifier is absent even though every protocol, identity, delegation, route, resource, token, policy, and monitor binding matches.
